title: AI Wrote Swift Code That Looked Fine… Until Xcode Instruments Exposed It
summary: Antoine van der Lee profiles an AI-generated Swift wallpaper app whose correct-looking output hides hangs, actor-isolation bottlenecks, and unnecessary suspension points. An iOS team can use Instruments to measure each concurrency change, compare release-build traces, and reject generated code that compiles but does not meet performance expectations.
takeaway: Treat Instruments traces as acceptance evidence for AI-written concurrency code; verify hangs, task lifetimes, actor isolation, and queue behavior before shipping.
